title_en: The Wind That Kept No Time: The Fall of Galloping Gertie
title_zh: 不合拍的风：塔科马大桥的陨落
english_paragraphs: On the morning of 7 November 1940, a sustained wind of about 40 miles an hour set the Tacoma Narrows Bridge twisting. Its deck tilted from side to side in ever more violent oscillations until most of the main span tore apart and tumbled into the water. No one died. Footage of the spectacle would later fascinate students worldwide.

The bridge had opened in July 1940 as the third-longest suspension span in the world at the time, its roadway hung from steel cables. Girders only eight feet deep stiffened the deck, making it slender, elegant, and economical, but far from rigid. Even faint breezes made it heave, earning the nickname Galloping Gertie.

Textbooks have long invoked resonance: a periodic push that matches an object's natural frequency can amplify its motion, as when well-timed shoves propel a child on a swing. The analogy is intuitive but deceptive. That morning's wind did not pulse in time with the bridge; it blew fairly steadily.

The mechanism was subtler. Each twist altered the passing airflow, which reinforced the next twist: a feedback loop that kept tapping the wind for energy. In March 1941 a federal panel blamed the deck's flexibility and wing-like lift. Later analysis called the mechanism flutter; in February 1991 two engineers asserted in a physics journal that textbooks had erred.

The panel urged wind-tunnel tests, and trials on scaled-down replicas gradually became customary for suspension bridges. A sturdier replacement opened in October 1950. Gertie's fall may still instruct engineers, if read accurately: the wind never kept time with the bridge, the bridge's own motion turned a sustained wind destructive.
chinese_paragraphs: 1940年11月7日上午，时速约40英里的持续大风使塔科马海峡大桥开始扭转。桥面左右倾斜，振荡越来越剧烈，最终主跨的大部分断裂，坠入水中。无人遇难。这场景象的影像，后来吸引了世界各地的学生。
大桥于1940年7月通车，其悬索桥跨径当时位居世界第三，路面由钢缆悬吊。桥面只靠高八英尺的钢梁加强，因此显得纤细、优美又经济，却远不够刚硬。即使微风也会让它起伏，因而得了“奔腾的格蒂”这个绰号。
教科书长期用共振来解释这起事故：如果周期性的推力与物体的固有频率相合，就能放大运动，就像踩准节拍推秋千上的孩子。这个类比直观，却会误导人。那天上午的风并没有跟着大桥的节拍一阵阵吹来，而是相当平稳。
实际机制更微妙。桥面每一次扭转都会改变掠过的气流，气流又加强下一次扭转，形成不断从风中获取能量的反馈回路。1941年3月，一个联邦调查委员会把事故归因于桥面的柔性和类似机翼的升力。后来的分析把这一机制称为颤振；1991年2月，两位工程师在一份物理学期刊上指出，教科书的解释错了。
委员会力主做风洞试验，此后用缩尺模型测试悬索桥逐渐成为惯例。更坚固的新桥于1950年10月通车。只要读懂真正的机制，格蒂的倒塌仍能给工程师以启示：风从未与桥合拍，是桥自身的运动，让一股持续的风变得具有破坏力。

illustration_prompt:
Create a single publication-quality landscape 3:2 narrative illustration for an adult illustrated English-reading booklet. Finished standalone artwork, not a book mockup, not a collage of multiple unrelated panels. Sophisticated contemporary editorial gouache and watercolor, carefully controlled colored-pencil accents, velvety matte paint, subtle warm paper texture, soft natural daylight. Warm ivory paper dominates; subdued eucalyptus and sage greens structure the composition; restrained buttery lemon-yellow and dusty terracotta accents. Calm, comfortable, refined, credible drawing and natural anatomy. An airy coherent composition with one clear story focal point and at most two supporting details, generous breathing room at all edges and softly feathered painted edges into ivory. Detailed but uncluttered. Historically and scientifically appropriate objects, clothing and setting. Show the particular article's pivotal event or mechanism rather than a generic portrait or generic textbook symbols. Human figures treated with dignity; no grotesque caricature, no sensational violence or visible injuries. For disasters, emphasize the setting, evidence or human response without graphic suffering. For uncertain scientific claims, depict the observations and investigation without presenting debated mechanisms as proven. Absolutely no typography, captions, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, diagram labels, fake writing or invented charts anywhere. Do not render invisible forces as literal magic. Avoid corporate vector icons, slick 3D rendering and childish cartoon style. High-quality, print-ready visual storytelling, matching a warm ivory-and-sage adult watercolor booklet.

ARTICLE-SPECIFIC SCENE:
A coherent historical view of the original narrow Tacoma Narrows suspension bridge over the quiet grey-sage waters of Puget Sound on a windy morning in 1940. The central focal section is the slender steel roadway undergoing a credible torsional twist: one side of a short middle section tilts upward while the other tilts downward, and the neighboring sections remain physically connected. Two upright steel towers and correctly anchored suspension cables establish the engineering form; the deck must not become a ribbon loop or an impossible broken roller-coaster. No cars or people in danger, no explosion, no fantasy wind arrows or vibration labels. A spare wooded shoreline is the only supporting environmental detail. This depicts wind interacting with a flexible bridge, not a rhythmic person pushing it; no swing, musical notes or repeated wave diagrams. Serious airy watercolor with muted sage steel and ivory sky.

IMPORTANT HISTORICAL CORRECTION TO THE REFERENCE IMAGE: This must be the ORIGINAL 1940 Tacoma Narrows Bridge. Remove every deep triangular open-web truss under the roadway, including the large triangular hump near the center. The original bridge had slender continuous SOLID PLATE GIRDERS approximately eight feet deep, not a deep lattice truss. Keep the watercolor palette, landscape proportions, towers, cables and distant shoreline. Redraw the thin roadway with credible TORSION: at one short central stretch the nearer edge tilts downward and the farther edge tilts upward, so the road surface is visibly tilted side-to-side; preserve structural continuity and do not merely draw a vertical roller-coaster hump. The thin solid side girders twist with the deck. Both main suspension cables must follow smooth anchored curves, not bent angular peaks. No lettering, diagrams, arrows, vehicles or people. This is an engineering-history illustration of the flexible 1940 bridge before collapse, not the deeper and stiffer 1950 replacement.
approved_summary: 1940年，刚通车数月的塔科马大桥在持续大风中剧烈扭转、断裂坍塌，无人遇难。
轻巧经济的桥面刚度不足，连微风都能使其起伏，早已有“奔腾的格蒂”之名。
课本常用共振解释事故，但当天的风相当平稳，并没有按桥的节拍反复推它。
桥的扭转改变气流，气流又加强下一次扭转，不断从风中取能；这一机制称为颤振。
事故推动悬索桥模型风洞试验成为惯例；更坚固的新桥于1950年通车。
